title: Specify directory for temporary captures
description:
Add a capture option `--temp-dir` to wireshark/tshark/dumpcap that
specifies the directory in which temporary capture files are to be
written. If not specified, uses the system default behaviour.

Add a GUI element in the capture options dialog for specifying this
directory.

I found that this couldn't be effective as a user preference; it had to
be a capture option in order to be successfully propagated to dumpcap
child processes.

A lot of internal function signatures were changed so that the directory
location could ultimately be passed to `create_tempfile()`. 

Closes #16432

notes.body: If this depth of change is more than desired, then a simpler approach would be to keep only the changes in `tempfile.c` and have it use the `TMPDIR` environment variable as its condition of using the alternate logic.

`S_IRWXU` is [not defined on Windows](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/13575543/why-arent-s-irwxg-and-s-irwxo-defined-in-sys-types-h-on-windows), that's why the build is failing.
It can be defined, I think, if `sys/types.h` is included. The ones with groups definitely don't exist even including that. I'm not a Windows dev, but did try to compile it.

Including `sys/types.h` or `sys/stat.h` didn't help on my Windows test. I see two possible approaches:

1. Test if `S_IRWXU` is defined and define it to `0700` if not
2. Disable the test for a writable directory (possibly only on Windows or only if `S_IRWXU` isn't defined)
I went with the second approach in 3550ffd5.

I would avoid a reset functionality here. The setting could be As far as I understand it, the tempdir is set on starting Wireshark or for a capture and as a more permanent solution. Or is the idea here to set it per capture? What is the use case for that, would it not be sufficient to capture and save it after stop?

Anyway, I think a browse button is sufficient, reset is not really necessary.

I must admit, I find this functionality very useful on the command-line. But I fail to see a bigger scenario for it in the UI. Would the use case be, that the user may not write to the default location? In such a case a lot of programs would have issues for that. Or would the use case be, that the user has a certain output directory per task and use this to temporarily set another? In such a case - as it is temporary - a simple option for the cli as well as in the ui (without the need for resetting) would be sufficient as well in my opinion. 

I think this can be a useful feature, though

Ok, last thing, I agree it should not be a capture option, but I cannot see another good solution either. But for me, the only thing remaining is the reset button. It just makes no sense. The user will set it once, and there is no need to reset it and if so, he can set it to the system settings using the dialog anyway. The reset button is something we need to manage and I would love to avoid code which is not really necessary.

Drop the button and it can be merged in my opinion. Unless you know a good argument for an explicit reset functionality, except for convenience.

commits_data.title: Guard `S_IRWXU` use behind `#ifdef`
commits_data.message:
Guard `S_IRWXU` use behind `#ifdef`

The test for a writable directory does not work on Windows since
`S_IRWXU` is not defined there. Removing the test is not ideal but also
not harmful; the capture will still fail for the obvious reason if it
tries to write to a nonwriteable directory.
